finding_key: packages/backend/src/auth/github.strategy.ts::the renamed `__clistatetoken` → `__oauthstate` handoff from guard to strategy is not covered by any test
evidence: In `packages/backend/src/auth/github.strategy.ts` the new `authenticate` reads `(req as { __oauthState?: string }).__oauthState` and assigns `opts.state`; the only writer is `github-auth.guard.ts` (`req.__oauthState = stateToken` / `= this.startWebState(context)`), and both sides use untyped `req`/inline casts, so a divergent rename would compile silently and, per the strategy's own comment about passport-oauth2's always-succeeding `NullStore`, would ship an authorization request with no CSRF binding. The diff adds `github-auth.guard.spec.ts` (writer side only) and extends `auth.controller.spec.ts` (callback/exchange side only); it adds or modifies no test that invokes `authenticate` or inspects `opts.state`, so the guard→strategy handoff is indeed uncovered by this change. I could not read the pre-existing `github.strategy.spec.ts` (empty working directory, file not supplied), so the claim that it asserts only endpoint URLs is inferred from the fact that the rename required no edit to it — strong but indirect. Scored minor because this is a missing regression test on a security-relevant seam rather than a defect in the shipped behavior.
